chunks: He said: Abu Ubaydillah Muhammad ibn Imran al-Marzbani reported to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Jawhari narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar informed us, saying: Ali ibn Salih informed me, saying: Abdullah ibn Mus'ab narrated to me, from his father, who said:

Abdullah ibn Abbas attended the assembly of Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan. Mu'awiya turned to him and said: 'O Ibn Abbas, you people wish to monopolize the Imamate just as you were privileged with Prophethood! By Allah, these two will never come together. Your argument about the Caliphate is dubious to the people. You say: We are the People of the House of the Prophet, peace be upon him, so why should the succession to the Prophethood be outside us? This is a specious argument, because it resembles the truth and has a touch of justice, but things are not as you imagine. The Caliphate rotates among the clans of Quraysh according to the will of the public and the consultation of the elite. We do not find people saying: If only Banu Hashim ruled us, for had they ruled us it would have been better for us in this world and the hereafter. And if you had truly renounced it yesterday as you claim, you would not have fought for it today. And by Allah, had you held power, O Banu Hashim, the ill wind of Ad and the thunderbolt of Thamud would not have been more destructive to the people than you.'

Ibn Abbas, may Allah have mercy on him, replied: 'As for your saying, O Mu'awiya, that we argue based on Prophethood for our entitlement to the Caliphate — by Allah, it is indeed so. If the Caliphate is not deserved through Prophethood, then by what is it deserved? As for your claim that Caliphate and Prophethood do not combine for anyone, then where is the word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty? Indeed, We gave the family of Ibrahim the Book and the Wisdom, and We gave them a mighty sovereignty." The Book is the Prophethood, the Wisdom is the Sunnah, and the sovereignty is the Caliphate. We are the family of Ibrahim, and that decree continues among us until the Day of Resurrection. As for your claim that our argument is dubious — that is not so. Our argument is brighter than the sun and more luminous than the moon. The Book of Allah is with us and the Sunnah of His Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, is within us. And you know that well, but pride has turned you away, and haughtiness has made you stiff-necked because we killed your brother, your grandfather, your maternal uncle, and your paternal uncle. So do not weep over decaying bones and souls perishing in the Fire. And do not be angry over blood that was spilled by polytheism, made lawful by disbelief, and placed by the religion.'

As for the people's refusal to give us precedence in the past and their turning away from consensus upon us — what they have been deprived of from us is greater than what we have been deprived of from them. In every matter, when its outcome is achieved, its truth is established and its falsehood vanishes. As for your pride in this transitory kingdom to which you ascended through vain trickery — Pharaoh had such a kingdom before you, and Allah destroyed him. O Banu Umayya, whatever you rule for a day, we shall rule after you for two days; whatever you hold for a month, we shall hold for two months; whatever you possess for a year, we shall possess for two years. As for your saying that if we had ruled, our rule would have been more destructive to the people than the wind of Ad and the thunderbolt of Thamud — the word of Allah belies you in that. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: "And We did not send you except as a mercy to the worlds." We are the nearest members of his household, and the mercy of Allah upon His creation through His Prophet is manifest, while the torment of your seizing the necks of the Muslims is manifest for all to see. And after you, the rule of your son and the sons of your father shall be more destructive to creation than the barren wind. Then Allah shall take vengeance through His saints, and the final outcome shall be for the God-fearing.

ai.seo_question: What was the debate between Abdullah ibn Abbas and Mu'awiya about the Caliphate and Imamate?
ai.summary: This narration records a famous theological debate between Abdullah ibn Abbas and Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan about the right to the Imamate and Caliphate. Mu'awiya argued that Prophethood and political authority cannot combine in one family, and that the Banu Hashim's claim is dubious. Ibn Abbas systematically refuted each point using Quran 4:54 (which grants the family of Ibrahim sovereignty alongside the Book and Wisdom) and Quran 21:107 (which describes the Prophet as a mercy to the worlds), establishing the Ahl al-Bayt's divinely-ordained right to leadership.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 4. He said: Abu Ubaiydillah Muhammad ibn Imran al-Marzbani reported to me from Muhammad ibn Husayn al-Jawhaeri, who reported from ‘Ali ibn Sulaiman who reported from al-Zubair ibn Bakkaar, who reported from ‘Ali ibn Swaleh, who reported from Abdullah ibn Mas’ab, from his father that

Abdullah ibn Abbas called upon Mua’wiya ibn Abi Sufyan, who welcomed him, and then said: "O Ibn Abbas, you people wish to restrict Imamat (to yourselves) the way you have been privileged with Prophethood? By Allah, these two will never go together. Your argument about the Caliphate has put people in doubt. You say: ’We are Ahlul Bayt of the Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, then why should the succession to the Prophethood be outside us?’ This creates suspicion, for it has a semblance of truth, and a touch of justice. But things are not the way you imagine. The Caliphate has to rotate in various tribes of Quraish according to the general will of the public and the consultation of the selected ones. And we do not find people saying: ’We wish we were ruled by Banu Hashim, for if they did, we would have been better off here and hereinfter.’ And if you had stayed away from it yesterday the way you claim, you would have fought for it today. And By Allah, if you had acquired the rulership, O Banu Hashim, then the ill wind of A’d and the thunderbolt of Thamood would not have been worse killer of men than you."

So Ibn Abbas replied (May Allah bless him with mercy): "O Mu’awiya, when you said that we base our argument on the Prophethood to prove our eligibility for Caliphate, then, by Allah, it is of course as you say. For if the Prophethood does not provide eligibility to the succession (Caliphate), what else does? And when you say that Caliphate and Prophethood do not combine for anyone, then what would say about the verse in which Allah, Most High, Says: ’Do they envy the people for the bounty that Allah has given them by His Grace. Yet We gave the family of Ibrahim the Book, and the Wisdom and We gave them a mighty sovereignty.’ (al-Nisa, 4:54) So, the Book is the Prophethood, the Wisdom is the Sunnah, the Traditions of the Prophet, and the sovereignty is the Caliphate. And we are the descendants of Ibrahim, and that is why the order remains applicable for us till the Day of Judgement. As for your claim that our arguments are dubious, then that is not true. Our arguments are brighter than the sun, and more luminous than the moon. The Book of Allah is with us, and the Traditions of the Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, are within us. And you know that very well, but pride makes you turn away; and you hold your head in haughtiness because we killed your brother, your grandfather, your maternal uncle and your father’s brother. Well, do not shed tears over the rotten bones, and upon the souls which are perished in hell-fire; and do not be vengeful for the blood spilled in the way of polytheism, made lawful by unbelief, and is debased by the religion (Islam).

And as for the people who refused to give us preference and turned away from granting us their consensus, be it clear that what they have lost from us is greater than what we have lost from them! In every matter, the truth is established and the untruth is dispelled when the result is obtained. And as for your pride in this transitory kingdom to which you have ascended by trickery, (remember that even) Pharaoh had such kingdom before you, and Allah destroyed him. O Banu Umayya, what you hold under rule for a day, we may hold it for two days after you; and what you have for a month, we may have it for two months, and if for a year, then we may hold it for two years. And when you said that if we were the authority, our rule would have been a worse killer of men than the ill wind of A’d and the thunderbolt of Thamood, that statement has been belied by Allah, the Most High, in the Qur’an: ’And We did not send you but as a mercy to all beings.’ (al-Anbiya, 21:107) As we are the nearest inmates of the Prophet’s household, our mercy over the creatures of Allah is evident; and the torment of your kingdom over the people is there for everyone to see. And after you have gone, the kingdom will be in the hands of your son and your brothers - and that will be a worse killer of people than the fatal wind. Then Allah will avenge through His devotees, and the final success is for the pious."
